questions.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $a=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ If $x=y+z,$ where $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ then $z=$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072287/assets/d887852fe51f08cb7296437e69b6a9632721cfd155558e6abf9a99b4f59f7ad6.png)

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{a}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x & =\frac{a\cdot x}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5+3\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot (-1)+6\cdot 4}{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{30+3+3+24}{36+9+9+36}a \\  & =\frac{60}{90}a \\  & =\frac{2}{3}a \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ z & =x-{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ as shown in the picture above.

In conclusion, $z=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Find the distance between $x$ and $\text{Span}{b}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The distance between the vector $x$ and the vector space $\text{Span}{b}$ is given by $‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖$, where $\overset{^}{x}$ in the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{span}{b}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{b}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{b\cdot x}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot 2+1\cdot (-2)+(-1)(-2)}{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-2-2-2+2}{1+1+1+1}b \\  & =-b \\  & =-1[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{((-2)-(-1))^{2}+(2-1)^{2}+((-2)-(-1))^{2}+((-2)-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1+9} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector onto the Solution Space of a System of Equations
questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of  linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{10}{10}b \\  & =b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find the distance between $x$ and $\text{Span}{b}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The distance between the vector $x$ and the vector space $\text{Span}{b}$ is given by $‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖$, where $\overset{^}{x}$ in the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{span}{b}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{b}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{b\cdot x}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 3+1\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot (-2)+0\cdot (-2)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{6+4+2}{4+1+1}b \\  & =\frac{12}{6}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-4)^{2}+(4-2)^{2}+(-2-(-2))^{2}+(-2-0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4+0+4} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector onto the Solution Space of a System of Equations
questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-4)\cdot (-3)+8\cdot 1}{{(-3)}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{20}{10}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
